items.t: — A 22-carat gold Cadbury 'Conundrum' egg made by Garrard & Co. in 1983 sold for £123,500, about $166,600, at Batemans Auctioneers & Valuers in Stamford on 1 August, reported by Forbes on 8 August and called a world auction record for a bejewelled egg of its type. It made close to six times its estimate and about eighteen times the £6,500 it took at its previous sale. The catalogue puts the egg at 323.6 grams of 22-carat gold, roughly $41,400 of bullion at Friday's close, a metal figure derived by this desk. Forbes dates the earlier sale to 2018 and the catalogue entry is dated July 2017; both are carried

— The People's Bank of China added 640,000 troy ounces of gold in July, about 19.9 tonnes, the largest single month since October 2023's 740,000 ounces and the twenty-first consecutive month of buying. Holdings reached 76.08 million ounces at the end of July from 75.44 million at the end of June, roughly 2,366 tonnes against 2,346. The gold reserve was valued at $306.35 billion inside total foreign-exchange assets of $3.419 trillion, about 8%. Against this paper's own reporting of 33 tonnes across the whole second quarter, July alone runs at close to double that monthly pace

— Spot markets did not trade over the weekend and the mark of record is unchanged for a second day: gold $4,341.30, silver $63.46, platinum $1,743.00, palladium $1,357.00, all from Kitco's 5:00pm New York close on Friday 7 August. The Editor re-read Kitco at press time and the page returned the identical Friday close, matching the 05:00 tape exactly, so the tape stands unamended and this edition prints the number the tape carries. Fine gold remains $139.58 a gram

— Shanghai Gold Exchange Au99.99 traded at 938 yuan a gram on the morning of 8 August, up 7.53 yuan on the day. Chow Tai Fook listed 24-carat jewellery at 1,286 yuan a gram the same day, Chow Sang Sang 1,285, Lukfook 1,284, Lao Feng Xiang and Lao Miao 1,283, Zhou Liu Fu 1,281 — a spread of 348 yuan, about 37% over the benchmark, with every brand inside five yuan of the others. The same tally puts Shuibei wholesale to top brand counter at 170 yuan a gram. Brands raised counter prices by close to 60 yuan in a single session on 6 August. This is the figure the paper pulled on 7 August for want of verification

— Federation of the Swiss Watch Industry figures for the first half put exports to Turkey at 165.2 million francs, up 6.9% from 154.5 million, the seventeenth largest market. The United States fell 14.8%, Germany 10.5%, China 5.0% and Japan 1.6%, while India rose 31.5%, Mexico 14.9%, South Korea 6.5%, the United Kingdom 5.8%, Hong Kong 3.3% and the UAE 1.6%. France rose 63.4% on a logistics reclassification. Precious-metal watches fell 6.5% and steel 6.5% while bimetallic rose 20.0%; seven million wristwatches shipped, up 2.3%, on a value down 0.6%

— Kalyan Jewellers reported consolidated revenue of ₹10,589 crore for the June quarter, up 46% from ₹7,268 crore, and net profit of ₹349 crore, up 32%, announced 4 August. India same-store sales grew about 28%, international revenue 35% and the digital business Candere 112%, across 524 showrooms with 354 Kalyan-branded in India. The company says its Shine with India gold-recirculation campaign contributed more than 46% of revenue in the quarter and more than 55% in June alone

items.b: A COIN MADE OF OLD GOLD
items.t: — MMTC-PAMP, India's only LBMA Good Delivery refiner of gold and silver, launched a limited-edition 10-gram commemorative coin on 4 August struck entirely from 999.9-plus recycled gold, capped at 8,000 pieces in assayer-certified packaging with unique identification numbers, unveiled in New Delhi by the Olympic medallist Mirabai Chanu. A refiner selling recycled provenance as a feature rather than disclosing it as a compromise is a change of position, and it lands in the same month a listed retailer reports nearly half its revenue resting on the same metal

— P N Gadgil Jewellers replaced its lightweight diamond line Litestyle with a new brand, YOOU, on 8 August, offered in 9, 14, 18 and 22-carat gold and positioned for everyday rather than occasion wear. It trades through 13 exclusive outlets across Maharashtra and Goa plus shop-in-shop counters in five states, against a stated target of 100 stores by 2030. Sara Tendulkar continues as ambassador. The parent reported first-quarter revenue of ₹2,413 crore, up 41%, and plans roughly 103 store openings across its whole portfolio by the end of the financial year

— Six slate items were killed on verification. China's first-half gold demand mix (jewellery down about 30%, bar and coin up about 31%) is a confirmed repeat, published here twice, on 3 August from the World Gold Council and on 7 August from the China Gold Association. A claimed SGE withdrawal figure of 161 tonnes for August traces to LBMA Alchemist issue 111, published October 2023 about August 2023 — a date trap, killed. A claimed PBoC purchase of 2 tonnes in August, a tenth consecutive month, was wrong on figure, month and streak; the verified July print appears above. Titan's first-quarter earnings and Chow Tai Fook's Macau same-store figure are both confirmed repeats. Israel's first-half export figures were dropped: the readings do not reconcile, at $625.7 million polished against $1.77 billion polished for the same half, and the reporting is twelve days old. Gemstones is dark for a fifth consecutive edition and diamonds for a second, the latter on a collapse in reachable sources rather than an empty beat. Sotheby's Arcade Hong Kong closed 6 August and has published no result for a fourth day. UAE retail gold is reported at 523.25 AED a gram for 24-carat on 8 August by one Arabic outlet, carried here with the caveat that three outlets stood AED 7.25 apart on the same session two days earlier. On the diamond lines NAT1 and LGD1 carry unchanged; the lab-grown reference reads $711 on CaratRadar, dated today, against $511 on StoneAlgo dated 7 August, a gap of roughly 39% this desk carries rather than reconciles. RAPI returned 403 for a fifth day and the Zimnisky rough index remains unreadable
